long_biography.plain_text:
An MBA project on a small party-hire business gave New Zealand investor Graeme Hart a working model for acquisitions. He targeted cheap, straightforward and underperforming companies selling everyday products. Substantial borrowing funded their purchase; tighter cash management and operational consolidation then generated the cash to service the debt.

The method mattered more than attachment to any single company. Rank combined related operations, disposed of peripheral assets and eventually floated or sold businesses after restructuring. A former partner described a disciplined rhythm of strategic reflection, advice from others, milestones and monitoring. That process enabled an Auckland investment company to direct a much larger international industrial group.
